feature: OpenType: Discretionary Ligatures
inp: No feature control.

feature: OpenType: Fractions
inp: No feature control.

feature: OpenType: Oldstyle figures
inp: No feature control.

feature: OpenType: Ordinals
inp: No feature control.

feature: OpenType: Swash
inp: No feature control.

feature: OpenType: Titling Alternates
inp: No feature control.

feature: OpenType: Stylistic Alternates and Stylistic Sets
where: Character panel OpenType buttons; Properties > Type Options
inp: No feature control.

feature: OpenType: Ornaments, Justification Alternates, proportional / tabular figures
inp: No feature control.

feature: OpenType submenu (Standard Ligatures, Contextual Alternates, Discretionary Ligatures, Swash, Oldstyle, Stylistic Alternates, Titling Alternates, Ornaments, Ordinals, Fractions, Justification Alternates, Japanese forms)
where: Type > OpenType; Character panel menu > OpenType
inp: No OpenType feature state or UI. Canvas text only gets Chromium's defaults (liga, calt, kern) and loses even those when tracking is non-zero (drawSpaced draws glyph by glyph). Needs a shaper with feature control (HarfBuzz wasm or opentype.js over font data from queryLocalFonts().blob()).

feature: OpenType: Contextual Alternates toggle
inp: No toggle; on by Chromium default only in the whole-line drawing path.

feature: OpenType: Standard Ligatures toggle
inp: No toggle. Ligatures appear by Chromium default when tracking is 0 and disappear when tracking is set, on a path and in stacked text.

feature: Favourite fonts (star) and favourites filter
inp: No favourites.

feature: Font menu WYSIWYG preview with selectable sample text
inp: Family names only, in the UI font.

feature: Live preview of a font on the canvas while hovering the list
inp: A native select cannot report hover; the change applies only on selection.

feature: Filter fonts by classification (Serif, Sans Serif, Script, Monospace, Decorative ...)
inp: No filter. Adobe's classification metadata is not available; a local equivalent can be derived from each font's OS/2 family class and PANOSE values.

feature: Recently used fonts at the top of the list
inp: No recents list.

feature: Variable fonts: named instances and axis sliders (weight, width, slant, optical size, custom)
where: Properties panel / Character panel for variable fonts
inp: No axis UI or font-variation data. An installed variable font only receives the five CSS weights from the style list.

feature: Font Preview Size (None, Small ... Huge)
inp: Font pickers are plain <select> elements (text.js typeOptions, character.js) with no sample preview at all, so there is nothing to size.

feature: Manage Missing Fonts / Replace All Missing Fonts / Resolve Missing Fonts
where: Type > Manage Missing Fonts; missing fonts dialog on open
inp: No detection: a family that is not installed silently renders in Chromium's fallback face, with no dialog, no layer badge and no substitution UI. The fallback font detector in text.js (detectFonts) could be reused to test availability.

feature: Font search by name
inp: Only the native select's type-ahead on the first letters; no substring search across family and style.

feature: Options bar: font family picker (search field, WYSIWYG list, filters)
inp: A native select of family names (typeOptions 'family'). No text search field, no preview, no filters, no recent list; only the select's type-ahead.

feature: Colour, emoji and SVG fonts
where: Font menu; Glyphs panel (EmojiOne, Trajan Color)
inp: 0.4: colour fonts and emoji drawn in colour, fallback to another installed font; OpenType-SVG glyphs draw as plain outlines

feature: Font style list showing the family's real styles
where: Options bar and Character panel: font style
inp: Fixed list of ten entries (Light, Regular, Medium, Bold, Black, each with Italic; STYLES in text.js) mapped to CSS weight/italic, whatever the family contains. Styles such as Condensed, Semibold, Display or Oblique are unreachable, and absent weights are synthesised by Chromium without telling the user. queryLocalFonts already returns style and postscriptName per face but only .family is read.

feature: Missing glyph protection (automatic fallback font for unsupported characters)
inp: Always on implicitly: Chromium substitutes a system fallback face per character. Not switchable and the substituted font is not reported.

feature: Show Similar Fonts
inp: Absent. Photoshop uses Adobe's trained visual-similarity model. Honest substitute: similarity from PANOSE/OS-2 metrics and measured glyph proportions of installed fonts.

feature: Fonts bundled with the application
where: Photoshop installation (Myriad, Minion, Source families, EmojiOne ...)
inp: Pigment ships no fonts (no @font-face or font files in src/renderer). Adobe's commercial families cannot be shipped; OFL families (Source Sans/Serif, Source Han, Noto, Noto Color Emoji) can be bundled so documents have a guaranteed default.

feature: System font list
inp: loadSystemFonts uses window.queryLocalFonts (main.js grants the 'local-fonts' permission) and falls back to probing 79 common families (detectFonts). bridge.localFonts is referenced but not implemented in preload.cjs, which is harmless.

feature: Check Spelling
inp: No command; the editor textarea sets spellcheck=false. Adobe's dictionaries are licensed; open Hunspell dictionaries (bundled, per language) with a Hunspell port are the offline substitute. Needs Ignore / Ignore All / Change / Change All / Add, Check All Layers and a per-text language.

feature: Find and Replace Text
inp: No command or dialog (Find Next, Change, Change All, Change/Find; Search All Layers, Forward, Case Sensitive, Whole Word Only, Ignore Accents).

feature: Double-click text with the Move tool to edit it
Placeholder text in new type layers (Lorem ipsum, pre-selected)
inp: 0.4: selected Lorem Ipsum, off in Preferences › Type

feature: Move the text while editing (Ctrl/Cmd-drag, or drag away from the text)
Tab characters
inp: 0.4: Tab types a tab, placed by the paragraph's tab spacing

feature: Transform while editing (Ctrl/Cmd shows the transform box: scale, rotate, skew the text)
inp: 0.4: scale, rotate and skew with Free Transform's box; distort and perspective are not offered while editing

feature: Cut, copy and paste text, with formatting kept between type layers
inp: 0.4: formatted clipboard between type layers, Paste Without Formatting

feature: Type keyboard shortcuts (size, leading, kerning/tracking, baseline, alignment, caps, super/subscript, scale reset)
inp: 0.4: Photoshop's type keys

feature: Resize the paragraph box while editing (eight handles)
inp: 0.4: eight handles; the box keeps its height and shows overflow

feature: Undo/redo inside an editing session
inp: 0.4: undo steps through typing and formatting runs; the commit is one History step

feature: IME and dead-key input (CJK, accents)
inp: 0.4: input methods and dead keys, composed text drawn in the layer

feature: Selecting text: drag, double-click word, triple-click line, quadruple-click paragraph, five clicks / Ctrl+A all
inp: 0.4: all of them; bidirectional text is selected in logical order

feature: Double-click the T thumbnail to edit and select all text
inp: panels/layers.js line 270 runs layer:edit-text, which activates the tool and selects all. Properties panel has an Edit Text button.

feature: Click existing text to edit, caret at the click
inp: hitTextLayer + caretIndex (works through the layer matrix, on a path and for stacked text).

feature: Editing overlay tracks zoom, canvas rotation and layer transform
inp: layoutEditor positions the textarea with the view matrix times the layer matrix and a measured CSS baseline; wheel events are forwarded so zooming while editing works.

feature: Cancel text (Esc)
inp: Esc and the cross button call cancelSession, restoring the snapshot or removing a new layer.

feature: Commit text (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, numeric Enter, tick, click outside, switch tool or layer)
inp: onEditorKey, deactivate, layer:activated listener and the options bar tick all call commitSession; one history entry per session.

feature: Keyboard navigation (arrows, word and line jumps, Home/End, Shift to extend)
inp: Native textarea caret movement; Home/End are re-implemented for path and stacked text (onEditorKey).

feature: Options bar: Cancel and Commit buttons
where: Type tool options bar while editing
inp: renderOptions adds the check and cross buttons during a session (commitSession / cancelSession).

feature: Overflow indicator (plus sign in the box handle)
Anti-aliasing method (None, Sharp, Crisp, Strong, Smooth, Windows LCD, Windows)
where: Type > Anti-Alias; Type tool options bar; Character panel
inp: No control anywhere and no field in the font object (DEFAULT_TEXT_STYLE in document.js). Canvas fillText always gives Chromium's greyscale anti-aliasing. None could be done by thresholding; Sharp/Crisp/Strong/Smooth are Adobe rasteriser variants and can only be approximated with an own glyph rasteriser (coverage gamma / emboldening). PSD import drops the antiAlias value.

feature: Warp Text (live, editable): 15 styles, Horizontal / Vertical, Bend, Horizontal Distortion, Vertical Distortion
where: Type > Warp Text; options bar Create Warped Text
inp: No warp property on TextLayer. The 15 presets with Bend/H/V do exist for pixels (WARP_PRESETS and presetControls in lib/warp.js, bezierWarp in shared/pixels/warp.js) but Edit > Transform > Warp asks to rasterise a text layer first (warp.js line 1308). Missing: Horizontal/Vertical axis switch, storing the warp on the layer and re-applying it after each text render, PSD import/export of the warp.

feature: Several character formats inside one text layer (per-character font, style, size, colour, decoration)
inp: 0.4: laid out and drawn by the HarfBuzz engine; PSD gets a layer with several styles as pixels until psd-text (0.5)

feature: Per-paragraph formatting inside one layer (alignment, indents, spacing per paragraph)
inp: 0.4: alignment, indents, spacing and the other paragraph settings per paragraph

feature: Text inside a closed shape or path (area type)
where: Type tool: click inside a closed path
inp: Clicking a path always starts text on the path (pathHit in text.js); there is no in-shape line breaker.

feature: Text on a path: baseline shift to move text off the path
where: Character panel baseline shift on path type
inp: layoutOnPath honours pathText.baselineShift and Image Size scales it, but no UI or command sets it.

feature: Text on a path: start and end brackets, drag to slide, drag across the path to flip
where: Path Selection / Direct Selection tool on type path
inp: A start-offset I-beam can be dragged, but only inside a Type tool editing session (hitOffsetHandle); no end bracket; flipping is the menu command text:flip-path, not a drag across the path; the Path Selection tool does nothing to it.

feature: Text on a path: create by clicking a path, type along it
inp: lib/text-path.js layoutOnPath: glyph-by-glyph placement on the flattened path, special cursor, Layer > Type > Text on Path to attach an existing layer. Limits: only the first subpath is used (admitted in ARCHITECTURE Known gaps), iteration is per UTF-16 unit so emoji and combining marks break, no kerning or ligatures, new lines are ignored, and the layer keeps a private copy of the path that cannot be reshaped with the Direct Selection or Pen tools afterwards (vector.js has no pathText target).

feature: Paragraph text in a bounding box (width and height)
inp: 0.4: width and height; text beyond the box is hidden

feature: Type on high-resolution and zoomed canvases
inp: Text is rasterised at document resolution and re-rendered live from parameters after Image Size (image-ops.js scales size, tracking, stroke and path) and Free Transform (matrix kept, text stays editable), as Photoshop does. Size limit 1296 px.

feature: Point text
inp: TextLayer with width null; click sets the baseline (beginNew).

feature: Indent left margin, indent right margin, first-line indent
inp: 0.4: Paragraph panel

feature: Justify last left / last centred / last right / justify all
inp: 0.4: all four; PSD keeps them

feature: Space before / space after paragraph
inp: 0.4: Paragraph panel

feature: Bulleted and numbered lists
inp: 0.4: bullets and numbering; the marker sits in the left indent and numbering runs within one layer

feature: Hyphenate, and the Hyphenation settings dialog
inp: 0.4: TeX patterns in eight languages and the Hyphenation dialog; Hyphenate Across Column has no effect (no columns)

feature: Reset Paragraph
inp: 0.4: Paragraph panel menu

feature: Roman Hanging Punctuation
inp: 0.4: Paragraph panel menu

feature: Justification settings (word, letter and glyph spacing min/desired/max, auto leading)
inp: 0.4: the Justification dialog; justified lines close up word spaces down to the Minimum

feature: Paragraph panel
inp: 0.4: Window › Paragraph and the Properties section

feature: Adobe Single-line Composer / Every-line Composer
inp: 0.4: both composers, with Unicode line breaking; Pigment's own Every-line algorithm, so lines can break differently from Photoshop's. East Asian Width is approximated

feature: Align left / centre / right
inp: font.align for the whole layer (TextLayer.renderBase, text on a path, stacked text).

feature: Options bar: alignment (left / centre / right, or top / centre / bottom for vertical)
inp: Segment control 'align' in typeOptions; applies to the whole layer; stacked vertical text maps it to top/middle/bottom (layoutStacked).

feature: Type tool context menu (Edit Type, Check Spelling, Find and Replace, Rasterize, Create Work Path, Convert to Shape, orientation, anti-alias, faux styles, Convert to Paragraph Text, Warp Text)
where: Right-click with a type tool or on a type layer
inp: No canvas context menu for type. The Layers panel context menu offers only generic items (Rasterize Layer, Convert to Smart Object, styles).

feature: Horizontal Type Mask tool
inp: No tool. Workaround today: make a text layer, Select > Layer Transparency as Selection (select:from-layer), delete the layer. A real tool needs the editing session to end in a selection instead of a layer, with the quick-mask overlay while typing.

feature: Vertical Type Mask tool
inp: No tool; same as the horizontal mask tool.

feature: Options bar: toggle text orientation button
inp: Not in typeOptions(); orientation is changed from Layer > Type or the Character panel.

feature: Alt-click to enter paragraph box width and height numerically
inp: 0.4: Alt-click asks for the box size

feature: Shift+T cycles the type tools
inp: Both tools share the 'text' slot and cycle with Shift+T (tools.js register); only two of Photoshop's four tools exist to cycle through.

feature: Options bar: toggle Character and Paragraph panels
inp: 0.4: the button toggles the panels

feature: Horizontal Type tool
inp: TypeTool 'type-horizontal' (lib/tools/text.js), shortcut T, click for point text, drag for a paragraph box, click existing text to edit.

feature: Paste Lorem Ipsum
inp: No command ('lorem' appears nowhere in src).

feature: Update All Text Layers
inp: No command. Relevant after PSD import (Pigment always re-renders text with its own engine instead of keeping the stored pixels) and after fonts change.

feature: Type menu as a top-level menu
inp: 0.4: Type menu between Layer and Select; some of its commands (Warp Text, Convert to Shape and others) come in 0.5

feature: Convert to Point Text / Convert to Paragraph Text
where: Type > Convert to Point Text / Paragraph Text
inp: Character panel 'Point text / Paragraph box' select plus box width (character.js setBox). No menu item. Paragraph to point just removes the width, so wrapped lines rejoin instead of becoming hard returns as in Photoshop.

feature: Type > Panels submenu (Character, Paragraph, Glyphs, Character Styles, Paragraph Styles)
inp: Only Window > Character exists (menu.js line 27, panels/character.js). No Paragraph, Glyphs, Character Styles or Paragraph Styles panel exists to list.

feature: Style overrides: plus indicator, Clear Override, Redefine by merging override
inp: Nothing to override.

feature: Load character and paragraph styles from another document
inp: Absent; PSD import does not read named style sheets either.

feature: Load Default Type Styles / Save Default Type Styles
where: Type > Load / Save Default Type Styles
inp: No character or paragraph styles exist, so no defaults file. The Character panel does persist last-used values as Type tool defaults (writeDefaults).

feature: Character Styles panel: create, apply, edit (Basic, Advanced, OpenType), duplicate, delete
inp: No panel and no style objects in the document model; depends on per-run formatting.

feature: Paragraph Styles panel: create, apply, edit (character formats, indents and spacing, composition, justification, hyphenation)
inp: No panel and no style objects.

feature: On-canvas glyph alternates popup for the selected character
inp: No alternates lookup (needs GSUB access) and no popup.

feature: Glyphs panel: grid of every glyph in the font, insert by double-click, zoom, font and style choice
inp: No panel. Needs the font's cmap and glyph table (font data from queryLocalFonts().blob() parsed with opentype.js or HarfBuzz).

feature: Glyphs panel: recently used glyphs
inp: No panel.

feature: Glyphs panel: subset filter (Entire Font, Alternates for Selection, Unicode ranges, OpenType categories)
inp: No panel.

feature: East Asian typography: Tsume, Aki, Mojikumi, Kinsoku Shori, Burasagari, character alignment, Warichu
where: Character and Paragraph panels with East Asian features
inp: None. Paragraph wrapping breaks at ASCII spaces only, so Chinese/Japanese paragraph text does not wrap at all.

feature: Middle Eastern and South Asian features: direction, digit type, kashida, justification alternates, diacritic positioning, ligature options
where: Character and Paragraph panels with Middle Eastern features
inp: No controls. Arabic/Hebrew are shaped and reordered by Chromium inside each drawn line only while tracking is 0; alignment and caret mapping (caretIndex measures prefixes left to right) are not direction-aware.

feature: Paragraph direction and World-Ready composers
where: Paragraph panel with Middle Eastern features
inp: No right-to-left paragraph setting.

feature: Language Options: Standard / East Asian Features / Middle Eastern and South Asian Features; text engine choice (Latin and East Asian vs World-Ready layout)
inp: No setting. Layout is one hard-coded path (space-delimited greedy wrap, left-to-right x placement).

feature: Text preserved as live text or vectors in PDF / SVG export
where: File > Save As Photoshop PDF; Export As SVG
inp: Text is exported as pixels in every format other than .pigment and PSD; no vector or live-text output.

feature: PSD import: text stays editable
inp: textLayerFromPsd (io.js) builds an editable layer from the first style run and first paragraph run only: family guessed from the PostScript name by regex (cssFamilyFromPsFont), bold/italic from the name or faux flags, size, colour, leading, tracking, underline, alignment, orientation, box width, matrix. Dropped: all further style runs, text warp, anti-alias, kerning, scales, baseline shift, caps, strikethrough, OpenType flags, box height, justification, indents, text on a path. Text is always re-rendered by Pigment, so it can look different from the stored Photoshop pixels.

feature: PSD export: text stays editable in Photoshop
inp: textToPsd writes one style and one paragraph style. Defects: font.name is the CSS family name, not a PostScript name, so Photoshop is likely to report a missing font or substitute; real bold/italic are written as faux; text on a path and stacked text are rasterised (io.js line 616), as is text in a Grayscale/ink view when its colour differs; no warp, no runs.

feature: Native format keeps text editable
inp: Text layers are serialised as parameters (document.json) including pathText and transform. Fonts are referenced by family name only; nothing warns when the family is absent on another machine.

feature: Character rotation and vertical-type glyph forms (vert/vrt2 punctuation, brackets)
inp: Stacked text draws the horizontal glyph forms upright, so CJK punctuation, long vowel marks and brackets are wrong in vertical text; no per-character rotation.

feature: Tate-Chu-Yoko (horizontal-in-vertical)
inp: Not supported by layoutStacked (one upright glyph per cell).

feature: Vertical type on a path
where: Vertical Type tool on a path
inp: Refused: setOrientation shows 'Text on a path is always horizontal'.

feature: Standard Vertical Roman Alignment
inp: Only as the all-or-nothing choice between 'Vertical' (everything rotated) and 'Vertical, Stacked' (everything upright) per layer; not per character.

feature: Vertical Type tool
inp: TypeTool 'type-vertical': creates horizontal text rotated 90 degrees clockwise by a layer matrix (letters sideways). Not a vertical layout; upright CJK needs switching the layer to 'Vertical, Stacked' afterwards.

feature: Orientation: Horizontal / Vertical
where: Type > Orientation; options bar toggle; Character panel menu Change Text Orientation
inp: text:orientation command (text-path.js setOrientation), Layer > Type radios and the Character panel Orientation select. 'Vertical' is the horizontal line rotated 90 degrees through the layer matrix (all glyphs sideways, CJK included); 'Vertical, Stacked' draws every glyph upright one em apart (Latin included). Photoshop mixes per script (CJK upright, Roman rotated unless Standard Vertical Roman Alignment). A CJK or mixed-script user would notice. Refused for text on a path.

feature: Actions record type layer creation and type edits
where: Actions panel while using the Type tool
inp: Type tool sessions are not recorded (USER-GUIDE: tool strokes are not recorded; layer:edit-text is in IGNORED_COMMANDS in actions/model.js). A 'Layer Is Type Layer' condition exists for conditional actions.

feature: Text variables and data sets (text replacement)
inp: No variables feature.

feature: Preferences > Type (smart quotes, missing glyph protection, show font names in English, Esc commits text, enable glyph alternates, recent fonts count, placeholder text, text engine)
inp: No type preferences in extras.js; Esc always cancels; quotes are typed as entered.

feature: Type units (points, pixels, millimetres) and point/pica size
inp: Only 'Ruler units' exists in Preferences; type is always in pixels.

feature: Convert to Shape
inp: No command. Same prerequisite as Create Work Path (glyph outlines), then build a ShapeLayer with the text colour.

feature: Create Work Path from type
inp: No command (grep finds none). Canvas API gives no glyph outlines; needs font file parsing (opentype.js/HarfBuzz) to emit glyph contours into doc.workPath.

feature: Extrude to 3D
where: Type > Extrude to 3D; options bar 3D button
inp: Absent; Pigment has no 3D (README 'What it does not do'). Adobe has retired Photoshop's 3D features, so this is lowest priority; an honest equivalent would be a bevel/extrude raster effect, not a 3D scene.

feature: Copy CSS / Copy SVG from a type layer
inp: No command.

feature: Free Transform on type keeps it editable (scale, rotate, skew, flip)
where: Edit > Free Transform on a type layer
inp: Matrix stored in layer.transform (image-ops.js); Distort and Perspective are refused for text as in Photoshop; Warp demands rasterising (see Warp Text).

feature: Masks and clipping on type layers
where: Layer > Layer Mask / Create Clipping Mask
inp: Generic layer features; text can be the clipping base or carry a mask.

feature: Type layer as smart object
where: Layer > Smart Objects > Convert to Smart Object
inp: layer:smart-convert accepts text layers (smart-object.js shiftLayer handles text); the text stays editable inside the smart object's contents.

feature: Type layer in the Layers panel (T thumbnail, name follows the text until renamed)
inp: Text badge, tooltip with the full text, automatic name from the first 30 characters while the name is still automatic (autoName in text.js).

feature: Filter the Layers panel to type layers
inp: layers-extras/find.js KINDS 'Type layers'.

feature: Rasterize Type Layer
where: Type > Rasterize Type Layer; Layer > Rasterize > Type
inp: layer:rasterize (layer-ops.js line 572) under Layer > Rasterize > Layer and the Layers context menu 'Rasterize Layer'; Rasterize All Layers too.

feature: Properties panel for a type layer (transform, character, paragraph, type options)
inp: 0.4: editable transform, character and paragraph sections

feature: Tool presets for the type tools
where: Options bar tool preset picker; Window > Tool Presets
inp: No tool preset system for type (the last-used options persist as defaults only).

feature: Contextual Task Bar for type (font, size, colour, style quick controls)
where: Floating task bar with a type layer selected
inp: No contextual task bar.

feature: Match Font
inp: Absent. Photoshop uses Adobe's trained recognition model and the Adobe Fonts catalogue. Honest substitutes: compare the selection against renders of the installed fonts (shape/feature matching, offline) or ask the user's own OpenAI/Gemini key to name candidate typefaces.

feature: Adobe Fonts filter, activation and automatic activation of missing fonts
inp: Needs Adobe's cloud service and subscription licence (README already states Adobe Fonts are out). Substitute: user-supplied font files and a clear missing-font dialog.

feature: More from Adobe Fonts
where: Type > More from Adobe Fonts; font menu cloud button
inp: Absent. Needs Adobe's font service and licence. Honest substitute: an 'Add Fonts...' command that loads user-supplied .ttf/.otf/.woff2 files into a Pigment fonts folder (FontFace API), and optionally bundled OFL families.

feature: Type in CMYK / Lab / Grayscale / 16- and 32-bit documents
inp: Text colour is always an 8-bit sRGB value and is not converted by a mode change (ARCHITECTURE: 'Text, shape, fill and adjustment layers are not converted'); the mode is only a view over it.

feature: Layer styles on live text
where: Layer > Layer Style on a type layer
inp: The compositor applies layer.styles to any layer type (compositor.js applyStyles), so Drop Shadow, Stroke, Bevel and the rest stay live on editable text. Pigment also has a non-Photoshop per-font stroke in the Character panel.

feature: Load a type layer's outline as a selection
inp: panels/layers.js line 245 and Select > Layer Transparency as Selection (select:from-layer).
